sn9.11:1.1: This short discourse offers a concise version of meditation advice given in more detail at [mn19]().
sn9.11:1.2: Even ascetics in the forest can be consumed by bad thoughts.
sn9.11:1.4: Trapped in a spiral of unwholesome thoughts, a meditator may feel guilty or worthless. But the deity has only compassion.
sn9.11:2.1: This term has already appeared at [sn4.4:2.1](), and plays a key role in dependent origination ([sn12.4:2.3]()). Their thoughts are irrational because they lead to the opposite of their goal, freedom.
sn9.11:3.1: Unwholesome thoughts are replaced by wholesome ones (cf. [mn20:3.1]()). The meditator is *not* urged to stop thinking; quietness is a process.
sn9.11:3.5: Suffering spurs on the practice, but the path itself is characterized by joy.
